title: There's a Moon Where Volcanoes Shoot Lava 200 Miles Into Space

scenes.text: There's a moon where volcanoes shoot lava 200 miles into space.
Jupiter's moon Io. Hundreds of active volcanoes. Nowhere in the solar system erupts more.
A NASA probe photographed one plume rising 200 miles. Three times higher than the edge of space.
Io is barely bigger than our Moon. But Jupiter's gravity kneads it until the ground rises and falls 330 feet.
That kneading heats it like bending a paperclip, until the rock melts.
Lava 200 miles high. On a moon the size of ours.

description:
Jupiter's moon Io is the most volcanically active world in the solar system, with hundreds of active volcanoes. In 2007, NASA's New Horizons probe photographed a plume from the volcano Tvashtar rising about 330 kilometres (200 miles) above the surface.
Io is only slightly larger than our Moon, but the tug-of-war between Jupiter's gravity and its neighbouring moons flexes its surface up and down by as much as 330 feet, heating the interior until rock melts.
Would you rather visit a moon of ice or a moon of fire? Comment below.
first_comment: Io's volcanoes paint the whole moon in yellow, orange and red sulphur, which is why it looks like a pizza in NASA photos. Which moon in the solar system do you find the weirdest?
